sm: Franklin Police public information manager Max Wynette hosts an episode about the Not in Our Mall holiday crime initiative. His guest is Sergeant Chris Harris, who oversees the department's flex unit. Harris describes his Army career, which ended with the rank of captain after service in Iraq. There he led a police transition team that helped build Iraqi police training and recruitment, including a lottery system to curb corruption, and then led a 42 soldier platoon doing security and convoy escort. He joined Franklin police around 2011, became a sergeant in 2023, and explains that flex is a small plainclothes unit of six to eight proactive officers who track crime trends, gather intelligence and work some vice and narcotics cases.

Harris says flex officers work closely as a team and set their own goals each day, unlike patrol officers whose days follow call volume. He says flex has helped support the city's rare murder investigations, and that the unit's drug detection dog Kobe is a big asset. He traces Not in Our Mall from an informal effort in the Cool Springs retail area to a deliberate partnership with retailers, mall security, patrol and traffic, and says it covers all retail across the city. The biggest current trend is tap to pay scams posing as donation requests, while shoplifting is mostly individuals, often from outside Tennessee, such as New York, Florida, Texas and Chicago. Shoppers will see signs, marked units and uniformed officers, while plainclothes officers in unmarked vehicles stay out of sight.

Harris says recent seasons have brought more firearm recoveries tied to shoplifting, along with drug arrests and outstanding warrants, and that arrests have leveled off at around 60 as large crews gave way to individuals and fraud. He urges shoppers and store staff to call when something looks suspicious, even if they are unsure. For patrons he advises locking car doors, not leaving gifts visible in cars, and keeping purses, wallets and phones with them, ideally while shopping in a group. The host mentions an ongoing investigation of a distraction theft in which a woman's credit card was taken from her purse. Harris adds that shoplifters have said they were told not to come to Franklin, mentions the holiday home check program, and gives the non-emergency dispatch number as 615 794 2513.
